questions.q: In the study of community safety, what is the most paramount **need for safety**?
options: To ensure that hospital wards are always full
To preserve human life, prevent avoidable injuries, and protect properties from destruction
To limit the speed at which the national economy grows
To restrict citizens from enjoying recreational activities
questions.explain: Safety measures are primarily implemented to **preserve life**, minimize hazards, and prevent the loss of properties resulting from accidents or carelessness.

questions.q: Consider the following actions. Which one correctly aligns with **safety measures in the home**?
options: Storing volatile fuels like petrol in the kitchen
Keeping sharp objects, medications, and toxic chemicals out of the reach of children
Leaving spilled water or oil on smooth tiled floors
Operating wet electrical switches barefoot
questions.explain: Children are vulnerable to domestic accidents. A critical safety measure is storing **sharp objects and chemicals securely out of their reach**.

questions.q:
Examine the following rules for a school environment:

| Location | Prohibited Action |
|---|---|
| Science Laboratory | Tasting unmarked chemicals |
| Staircases | $X$ |

Which of the following actions safely replaces $X$ to prevent injuries?
options: Walking in a single file
Holding the handrails
Playing, pushing, or running dangerously
Cleaning the steps
questions.explain: To maintain safety in schools, **playing, pushing, or running dangerously** on staircases must be heavily prohibited as it frequently leads to severe fall injuries.

questions.q: In industrial workplaces and construction sites, safety is highly dependent on workers using PPE. What does PPE stand for?
options: Personal Protective Equipment
Private Personnel Embezzlement
Protective Police Engagement
Public Property Evaluation
questions.explain: **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)** includes helmets, safety boots, gloves, and goggles, which are fundamental safety requirements for workers in hazardous environments.

questions.q: What is the standard, internationally recognized safety sequence a **pedestrian** must execute before crossing a busy road without traffic lights?
options: $$ \text{Look Right} \rightarrow \text{Run Fast} \rightarrow \text{Look Left} $$
$$ \text{Look Left} \rightarrow \text{Look Right} \rightarrow \text{Look Left again} $$ and cross when clear
$$ \text{Close Eyes} \rightarrow \text{Walk slowly} \rightarrow \text{Listen for horns} $$
$$ \text{Wave Hands} \rightarrow \text{Stop Vehicles} \rightarrow \text{Walk diagonally} $$
questions.explain: The fundamental pedestrian safety rule, especially in right-hand driving countries like Nigeria, is to **look Left, look Right, then look Left again**, ensuring the road is completely clear before crossing.

questions.q: To significantly reduce the occurrence of fatal head traumas during accidents, what is the most critical safety guideline for both **motorcyclists and their passengers**?
options: Wearing reflective jackets only at night
Holding onto the motorcycle firmly
Wearing properly fastened standard crash helmets
Riding on the pedestrian walkway
questions.explain: The skull is highly vulnerable during motorcycle accidents. Wearing a **standard crash helmet** is the legally required and most vital safety guideline to prevent traumatic brain injuries.

questions.q: Which of the following is an absolute safety contravention and highly dangerous practice for **motorists** (car drivers)?
options: Obeying the stipulated speed limits on the highway
Fastening seat belts before turning on the engine
Driving under the influence of alcohol and texting while driving
Using turn signals before changing lanes
questions.explain: **Driving under the influence of alcohol and texting** heavily impairs cognitive functions and reaction times, directly causing severe road traffic accidents and contravening safety guidelines.
